firewall.glossary.inbound: Someone or something out on the internet connected in to a service running on this PC.
firewall.glossary.outbound: This PC (or an app on it) reached out to a server elsewhere.
firewall.glossary.established: An active, currently open connection — data can flow both ways right now.
firewall.glossary.listen: This PC is waiting for incoming connections on this port, but nothing is connected yet.
firewall.glossary.syn_sent: This PC is trying to open a new connection and waiting for the other side to answer.
firewall.glossary.syn_received: The other side wants to connect and this PC acknowledged the request; the connection is being set up.
firewall.glossary.fin_wait_1: This PC asked to close the connection and is waiting for the other side to confirm.
firewall.glossary.fin_wait_2: The other side agreed to close the connection and this PC is waiting for its final close message.
firewall.glossary.closing: Both sides have asked to close the connection and are finishing the cleanup.
firewall.glossary.last_ack: The final close message was sent and this PC is waiting for the last acknowledgment before the connection fully ends.
firewall.glossary.delete_tcb: The connection is being removed from the system and its entry is being deleted.
firewall.glossary.closed: The connection is fully closed. Nothing is active anymore.
firewall.glossary.unknown: The connection state could not be determined.
firewall.glossary.time_wait: The connection just closed. Windows keeps it around briefly to make sure no leftover data arrives late.
firewall.glossary.close_wait: The other side closed the connection, and this PC is finishing cleanup on its end.
firewall.glossary.bound: A port reserved for use, but not actively listening or connected yet.
firewall.glossary.unverified: Not on a known-safe or known-bad list. Most everyday connections start out this way — it doesn't necessarily mean anything is wrong.
firewall.glossary.pid: Process ID — a temporary number Windows assigns to a running program while it is active.
firewall.glossary.whois: Looks up who owns/operates a given IP address, e.g. the company running that server.

settings.emergencyLockdown.label: Emergency Lockdown
settings.emergencyLockdown.desc: Enable emergency lockdown mode to quickly isolate the system from network threats
lockdown.title: Emergency Lockdown
lockdown.description: Instantly disable all network interfaces and stop non-essential services for emergency situations.
lockdown.confirmActivate: Are you sure you want to activate emergency lockdown? This will disable all network interfaces and stop non-essential services.
lockdown.confirmRestore: Are you sure you want to restore systems? This will re-enable network interfaces and restart services.
lockdown.warning: Warning: Emergency lockdown will disconnect you from the internet and stop background services. Use only in emergency situations.
lockdown.allowlist.title: Allowlist
lockdown.allowlist.description: Interfaces, services, and IPs listed here will remain active during lockdown. Use to maintain critical connectivity (VPN, management, backups).
